messages:
mel: Quick sync: we need a decision on shim lifecycle for the upcoming v2->v3 shape migration. Two patterns on the table: (A) short-lived edge adapter that normalizes traffic, (B) baked-in runtime shim with selective normalization. Pros/cons below, want calls from infra/obs/rt.

diego: Edge adapter wins for ownership boundaries. Keeps runtime surface stable and avoids expanding runtime test matrix. Tradeoff: extra network hop and more operational surface to monitor.

sara: Runtime shim benefits: single codepath, easier to guarantee cache key alignment and avoid duplicate validation. Con: runtime becomes responsible for many historical quirks; risk of cache fragmentation and harder rollbacks.

mel: Important non-functional requirements: 1) zero-silent-mutation (any transformation must be detectable via metadata) 2) deterministic checksum header `X-Shape-Checksum` for normalized requests 3) per-tenant rollout gating 4) observability hooks for both pre/post transform.

diego: Operational suggestion: make edge adapter the default, but implement a minimal runtime 'repair' mode that only triggers when `X-Repair-Needed: true` header present. That header would be set by the edge when it cant safely normalize (e.g., ambiguous multipart).

sara: Agree with header-based opt-in for runtime. Add tests: a) assert identical KV cache hit rates pre/post for canonicalized vs raw b) assert no widening of cache keys when runtime repair runs.

mel: Rollout cadence proposal: 1) create 3 cohorts: pilot (~50 tenants), ramp (500), GA. 2) pilot runs edge adapter only. If pilot uncovers >0.5% unknown-shape traffic or >5% latency delta at p95 we pause. 3) if edge adapter fails to normalize safely for >0.1% of requests, enable runtime-repair for those tenants only.

diego: Telemetry shape: emit `shim.transform` with fields (cohort, tenant, transform_type, latency_ms, checksum_in, checksum_out, repaired=true/false). Also `shim.failed_normalize` for variants.

ops-bot: ops-bot: canary deploy scheduled: `/deploy edge-adapter canary --cohort=pilot --version=2026-03-22-rc1`

sara: Security: Edge adapter must not drop or mutate auth headers. If normalization requires moving tokens, use ephemeral signed envelope with `X-Envelope-Sig` so runtime can verify authenticity.

mel: Cache strategy: post-normalization cache keys should include `shape_v` tag and the checksum. But we must avoid double-caching: runtime must prefer a canonical key precedence order: (shape_v, checksum) over legacy raw. Add an audit job to detect cache duplication daily.

diego: We need an emergency rollback plan: 1) flip cohort flag to `legacy` 2) edge adapter responds with `X-Adapter-Mode: off` 3) runtime fallback remains disabled unless explicitly toggled; ops team can toggle `runtime.repair=true` via feature-toggle service for hotfixes.

mel: Action items: diego -> implement edge adapter prototype + signed envelope design; sara -> CI matrix and cache-duplication tests; mel -> runbook + telemetry dashboard skeleton. Sync in 24h to lock decision. :eyes:
